evals.name: proposal-review
evals.prompt: Our platform team wants approval for the proposal in proposal.md (current directory). I'm the engineering manager who has to decide. Review it and write assessment.md: your assessment of whether we should adopt, what the proposal gets right or misses, whatever still needs answering before a decision, and a clear recommendation. Don't come back to me with questions in chat — put open questions in the file and I'll take them to the platform team.
evals.expected_output: assessment.md separates the technology's real power from its feature list; ties value to the concrete current-state pain (batch staleness, multi-week Jira export queue, morning reconciliation) rather than 'industry best practice'; flags the missing evidence of what the limitation costs as open questions; identifies the existing processes that would have to be retired; challenges the 'no process changes, batch runs in parallel indefinitely' plan as cost without benefit; and ends with a conditional recommendation rather than rubber-stamping adoption

evals.name: adoption-post-mortem
evals.prompt: Eighteen months ago we adopted CatalogHub, a data catalog. It has barely been used and leadership is asking why we're still paying for it — my notes are in catalog-notes.md (current directory). Write review.md: why the adoption failed to deliver, and what we should do now (renewal is next quarter). Don't ask me questions in chat — write anything that needs answering into the file.
evals.expected_output: review.md diagnoses the root cause as adoption without behaviour change: the old ways of finding data (emailing the platform team, #data-help) and documenting it (Confluence) were never retired, populating the catalog was optional, and nobody was asked to stop or change anything — so the org pays for the tool and the old process; it questions/confirms whether the underlying limitation (discovery bottleneck) is real using the 25-requests-a-week evidence; and it recommends a concrete decision for renewal: either make the catalog the enforced path (retire the parallel channels, make population part of the workflow) or decommission it, not more evangelism
